modules.summary: This tutorial introduces the fundamentals of computer networking, including network types, components, terminology, topologies, and practical applications that form the foundation for Cyber Security.
miniProjects: Draw the network layout of your school or college.
Identify different devices used in your home network.
Create a comparison chart of PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN.
commonMistakes: Assuming Internet and WWW are the same.
Mixing IP Address with MAC Address.
Ignoring the purpose of network protocols.
examTips: Remember full forms of PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN.
Understand the difference between Internet, Intranet and Extranet.

segments.title: Cyber Security Foundations & Cryptography
segments.summary: Master core cyber security principles, the CIA triad, ethical hacking methodologies, and cryptographic algorithms including RSA.

modules.title: Security Triad (CIA) & Case Studies
topics: Introduction to the CIA Triad
Confidentiality: Concepts and Controls
Threats to Confidentiality and Data Breaches
Integrity: Data Accuracy and Trust
Threats to Integrity and Hash Verification
Availability: Uptime and Fault Tolerance
Threats to Availability and Outages
Extended Security Models: Parkerian Hexad and Non-Repudiation
Balancing Security Controls with Usability
CIA Triad Implementation Case Studies
Evaluating CIA Trade-offs in Real-World Systems
learningOutcomes: Understand the core pillars of the CIA Triad.
Analyze threats affecting Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability.
Apply the CIA triad to real-world healthcare and financial systems.
Evaluate security trade-offs between protection and accessibility.

modules.title: Hacking, Ethical Hacking & Hacker Types
topics: Introduction to Hacking Concepts
Evolution of Hacking: From Curiosity to Cyber Threats
Ethical Hacking: Principles and Legal Frameworks
Hacker Taxonomy: White Hat Hackers
Hacker Taxonomy: Black Hat Hackers
Hacker Taxonomy: Grey Hat Hackers
Specialized Hackers: Red, Blue, and Purple Teams
Threat Actors: Nation-State, Hacktivists, and Script Kiddies
Legal vs Illegal Hacking: Cyber Law and Authorization
Role of Ethical Hackers in Enterprise Defense
Vulnerability Disclosure Programs and Bug Bounties
Ethical Hacking Case Studies and Industry Applications
learningOutcomes: Distinguish between malicious hacking and authorized ethical hacking.
Classify hacker categories and threat actor motivations.
Understand legal boundaries and compliance under cyber law.
Appreciate the defensive role of white-hat penetration testing.

modules.title: Phases of Hacking Methodology
topics: Overview of the 5 Phases of Hacking
Phase 1: Reconnaissance (Passive vs Active Footprinting)
OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence) Tools and Techniques
Phase 2: Scanning and Network Enumeration
Port Scanning, Banner Grabbing, and Vulnerability Scanning
Phase 3: Gaining Access (Exploitation Techniques)
System Exploitation, Buffer Overflows, and Credential Attacks
Phase 4: Maintaining Access (Backdoors, Rootkits, and Persistence)
Privilege Escalation and Lateral Movement
Phase 5: Covering Tracks (Log Tampering and Anti-Forensics)
Cyber Kill Chain vs MITRE ATT&CK Framework
Defensive Countermeasures across the 5 Hacking Phases
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the 5 standard phases of ethical hacking.
Analyze reconnaissance, enumeration, and exploitation techniques.
Identify persistence mechanisms, rootkits, and log cleaning methods.
Map hacking phases to modern defense frameworks (Cyber Kill Chain, MITRE ATT&CK).

modules.title: Cryptography, Watermarking & Cipher Types
topics: Introduction to Cryptography and Cryptanalysis

Steganography vs Digital Watermarking vs Cryptography
Real-World Applications of Cryptography and Watermarking
learningOutcomes: Explain cryptographic terminology and historical ciphers.
Differentiate between Symmetric and Asymmetric cryptographic algorithms.
Understand digital signatures and cryptographic hash functions.
Analyze digital watermarking techniques for copyright and asset protection.

modules.title: RSA Algorithm & Public Key Infrastructure
topics: Introduction to the RSA Algorithm and Asymmetric Security

Hybrid Cryptosystems: Combining RSA and AES
Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and Certificate Authorities (CAs)
Digital Certificates (X.509) and Trust Chains
Practical Implementations of RSA in SSL/TLS and SSH
learningOutcomes: Master the mathematical theory behind the RSA public-key cryptosystem.
Calculate RSA public and private keys using prime numbers and modular arithmetic.
Understand how PKI and digital certificates establish internet trust.
Evaluate RSA key length requirements against modern computing power.

segments.title: Information Security Management
segments.summary: Explore governance, risk management, ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS frameworks, security policies, and information security audit procedures.

modules.title: Introduction to ISM & Security Goals
topics: Introduction to Information Security Management (ISM)
Need and Importance of ISM in Modern Enterprises
Strategic Goals of Information Security
Information as an Organizational Asset
Roles and Responsibilities: CISO, Security Officers, and Custodians
The Three Dimensions of ISM: People, Process, and Technology
Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Drivers in ISM
Information Classification Schemes (Public, Confidential, Secret)
Data Lifecycle Security Management
Enterprise Security Culture and Awareness Programs
learningOutcomes: Understand the strategic purpose and scope of Information Security Management.
Identify key governance roles and organizational security responsibilities.
Apply data classification standards to protect critical enterprise assets.
Foster proactive security awareness and organizational resilience.

modules.title: ISMS Framework & Working Procedures

learningOutcomes: Explain the architecture and working procedure of ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS.
Apply the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle to maintain enterprise security.
Map ISO 27001 Annex A controls to technical and operational requirements.
Formulate Incident Response and Business Continuity strategies.

modules.title: Security Policies, Risk Assessment & Mitigation

Threat Identification and Vulnerability Assessment
Qualitative vs Quantitative Risk Analysis
Calculating Single Loss Expectancy (SLE) and Annual Loss Expectancy (ALE)
Risk Treatment Strategies: Mitigate, Transfer, Accept, Avoid
Risk Registers and Residual Risk Management
Third-Party and Supply Chain Risk Management
Threat Modeling Methodologies (STRIDE, DREAD)
Enterprise Risk Management Case Study
learningOutcomes: Draft and evaluate essential enterprise information security policies.
Conduct structured asset, threat, and vulnerability risk assessments.
Calculate quantitative risk metrics (SLE, ARO, ALE) and qualitative risk matrices.
Select appropriate risk treatment strategies for identified vulnerabilities.

modules.title: Information Security Auditing & Compliance
topics: Introduction to Information Security Audits

Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA)
Auditor Ethics and Professional Independence
Information Security Audit Case Study in Banking and FinTech
learningOutcomes: Explain the purpose, phases, and methodology of security audits.
Evaluate organizational compliance against industry standards (PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, DPDP).
Analyze audit logs and evidence to identify non-conformities.
Prepare comprehensive audit findings and corrective action reports.

segments.title: Cyber Attacks & Threat Analysis
segments.summary: Examine the technical mechanisms of active and passive cyber attacks, malware taxonomy, phishing, DoS/DDoS, SQL injection, social engineering, and landmark attack case studies.

modules.title: Passive vs Active Cyber Attacks

Passive Attacks: Traffic Analysis and Packet Sniffing
Characteristics and Challenges in Detecting Passive Attacks
Active Attacks: Modification of Messages and Data Tampering

learningOutcomes: Classify attacks into Active and Passive categories based on impact.
Understand technical mechanisms of sniffing, traffic analysis, and MitM.
Identify countermeasures including encryption, hashing, and mutual authentication.
Analyze attack vectors in enterprise network communications.

modules.title: Malware Taxonomy & Analysis

learningOutcomes: Categorize malware types according to infection, replication, and payload delivery.
Analyze the mechanics of Ransomware, Rootkits, and Botnet C2 servers.
Explain static and dynamic malware analysis methodologies.
Design layered malware defense using modern EDR and sandboxing technologies.

learningOutcomes: Understand psychological principles exploited in social engineering attacks.
Recognize various forms of phishing, vishing, smishing, and BEC attacks.
Identify insider threat indicators and technical exfiltration behaviors.
Implement technical protections (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and user training frameworks.

modules.title: Denial of Service (DoS) & DDoS Attacks
topics: Introduction to Denial of Service (DoS) Attacks

learningOutcomes: Differentiate between Volumetric, Protocol, and Application-layer DDoS attacks.
Explain the technical mechanisms of SYN flooding, Slowloris, and DNS amplification.
Evaluate defensive architectures including SYN cookies, CDN Anycast, and cloud scrubbing.
Analyze high-profile DDoS incidents and emergency mitigation procedures.

modules.title: Web Attacks, SQL Injection & Injection Defense

learningOutcomes: Understand the mechanics of SQL Injection and OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.

learningOutcomes: Analyze the root causes, attack paths, and repercussions of landmark global cyber attacks.
Evaluate supply chain vulnerabilities, zero-day exploits, and lateral movement tactics.
Formulate strategic incident response and disaster recovery takeaways.
Design defense-in-depth architectures resistant to modern Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs).

segments.title: Technological Aspects of Cyber Security
segments.summary: Implement and configure perimeter defenses, Firewalls, IDS/IPS, VPNs, SSL/TLS, IPsec, MFA, and explore AI, Blockchain, and Quantum Cryptography in cyber defense.

modules.title: Firewalls & Perimeter Defense Architectures
topics: Introduction to Network Perimeter Defense and Defense-in-Depth

Circuit-Level Gateways and Handshake Monitoring
Stateful Inspection Firewalls (Stateful Packet Inspection - SPI)
Application-Level Gateways (Proxy Firewalls)

learningOutcomes: Differentiate between Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) and Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS).

Understand deployment models (SPAN ports vs Inline appliances).

modules.title: Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) & Tunneling

Analyze the transition from perimeter VPNs to Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA).

modules.title: Network Security Protocols: SSL, TLS & IPsec
